[QUERENT] VroniPlag Wiki

[SYSTEM] The VroniPlag Wiki is a crowdsourced online platform hosted on [Fandom](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYQHrOzAVvh3CEJa5Hly3EaBdw8S5Vat9M96rqz6FrURl-bpoVkgcBpAkVxNQhkyyM9zto04GGDtBHJCqUuU4JDhLAVkbHewTMLHgWKPTBivcNsocB1P7b2Zi-3UqfKy6LWs) that investigates and documents academic plagiarism in German doctoral dissertations, habilitations, and scientific publications. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVQvB_JVDGfpp54JF6RL76EqD7KAESQ3377Kqf4XYLGBuDR2scWz2l_1xPPOOiwz4an09qsT1p3cyUWMelnHhHQY1IGy2cReWAoIp3mXJ-Sa0C-OXPmmDmElTN5LwD-9g), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYQHrOzAVvh3CEJa5Hly3EaBdw8S5Vat9M96rqz6FrURl-bpoVkgcBpAkVxNQhkyyM9zto04GGDtBHJCqUuU4JDhLAVkbHewTMLHgWKPTBivcNsocB1P7b2Zi-3UqfKy6LWs)]
Key Facts

* Launch Date: March 28, 2011
* Name Origin: Named after Veronica Saß (daughter of politician Edmund Stoiber), whose thesis was the first project documented ("Vroni" is a German nickname for Veronica).
* Scope: Documents hundreds of academic works with percentage breakdowns of copied text, side-by-side comparisons, and the status of university degree revocations.
* Process: Findings are officially reported to the relevant university's office of academic integrity before public release.
* Recognition: Awarded the Zedler-Preis für freies Wissen (Zedler Prize for Free Knowledge) by Wikimedia Germany in 2012. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESawHrOzAV9Fd7j63ywRpEm1FsW2xtr9_XvdM3JKnEWtSuXJJLGu0IN9lG4M4UvytDUlOx0-tgTxjTPTfVQ7mnp22FJrTNvYfyrnMfDGLFmNytGdLpC2qgPK_zgGVquvBYVzkryBzXdGiyIC1U), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVQvB_JVDGfpp54JF6RL76EqD7KAESQ3377Kqf4XYLGBuDR2scWz2l_1xPPOOiwz4an09qsT1p3cyUWMelnHhHQY1IGy2cReWAoIp3mXJ-Sa0C-OXPmmDmElTN5LwD-9g)]

transcript_class: CAPTURE-TIME VERBATIM RECORD — paste of the Overview expanded, with its source cards
d: VRONIPLAG WIKI, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a crowdsourced online platform hosted on Fandom that investigates and documents academic plagiarism in German doctoral dissertations, habilitations, and scientific publications.' Launch (28 March 2011), name (after Veronica Saß, daughter of Edmund Stoiber, the first case documented), scope (percentages of copied text, side-by-side comparisons, revocations), process (findings reported to the university's office of academic integrity before public release), recognition (the Zedler-Preis of Wikimedia Germany, 2012). Three cards: English Wikipedia, the wiki's home on Fandom, its Übersicht page ('Es dokumentiert 204 Disse…').
reading: The innocent reading first. The Overview identifies the wiki, its founding and name, what it documents and how it proceeds, and points to its home and its overview.
findings: THE ENTITY HELD. The date, Wikia (now Fandom) as host, the documentation of plagiarism in German theses and the notice to the university are the record's quotes from English Wikipedia. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the entity pages it saved.

THE WIKI'S OWN COUNT, IN A CARD. The record could not read the wiki (403 to a plain fetch on 2026-10-29) and took its count from German Wikipedia: 201 dissertations and 13 habilitation theses, as of 3 April 2023. The Übersicht card is the wiki's own page, truncated: 'Es dokumentiert 204 Disse…'. The composition does not give the figure; the card carries a later count than the record's, from the source the record could not reach.

WHAT IS NOT GIVEN. The method (each fragment classified and verified by a second person), the revocations (at least 90 doctorates, as of 30 April 2024) and the founder German Wikipedia names (Martin Heidingsfelder) are absent; 'the status of university degree revocations' gestures at the second.
THE PRIZE. The Zedler-Preis of 2012 is not in the record; unchecked.
analysis: A plagiarism wiki, itself an instrument of attribution, is composed from Wikipedia with its founding and procedure right. The capture adds to the record the one figure the record lacked from the wiki itself, through a truncated card.
per_note: Veronica Saß and Edmund Stoiber named (the first case, the name's origin); Wikimedia Germany and Fandom named; no identifier; the wiki's own pages cited.
